source.text: Ἔλεγον οὖν τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμιτῶν· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὃν ζητοῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι;

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore some of the Jerusalemites, "Not this [one] is whom they are seeking to kill?

en.L: So some of the people of Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not [the one] whom they are seeking to kill?
en.B: So some who lived in Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not the one they are out to kill?
en.R: Some people from Jerusalem itself said, "Is this not the man our leaders want to kill?

es.L: Decían, pues, algunos de los de Jerusalén: «¿No es este al que buscan matar?
es.B: Entonces algunos de los que vivían en Jerusalén decían: «¿No es este el que quieren matar?
es.R: Algunos que eran de la misma Jerusalén decían: «¿No es este el hombre al que nuestros dirigentes quieren matar?

fr.L: Certains des habitants de Jérusalem disaient donc : « N’est-ce pas celui-ci qu’ils cherchent à tuer ?
fr.B: Quelques habitants de Jérusalem disaient alors : « N’est-ce pas cet homme qu’ils veulent faire mourir ?
fr.R: Des gens de Jérusalem même ont dit : « N’est-ce pas l’homme que nos chefs veulent tuer ?

sw.L: Basi baadhi ya watu wa Yerusalemu walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si [yule] wanayetafuta kumwua?
sw.B: Basi baadhi ya wakazi wa Yerusalemu walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si yule wanayetaka kumwua?
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu wa Yerusalemu kwenyewe wakasema, "Je, huyu si yule mtu ambaye viongozi wetu wanataka kumwua?

vi.L: Vậy một số người ở Giê-ru-sa-lem nói: "Chẳng phải đây là [người] mà họ đang tìm giết sao?
vi.B: Vậy có mấy người dân Giê-ru-sa-lem nói: "Đây chẳng phải là người mà họ đang muốn giết sao?
vi.R: Một số người sống ngay tại Giê-ru-sa-lem nói: "Đây chẳng phải là người mà các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng ta muốn giết sao?

ko.L: 그러자 예루살렘 사람들 가운데 몇이 말하고 있었다. "이는 그들이 죽이려고 찾는 [사람이] 아니냐?
ko.B: 그래서 예루살렘에 사는 사람들 가운데 몇이 말했다. "이 사람은 그들이 죽이려고 하는 바로 그 사람이 아니냐?
ko.R: 예루살렘에 사는 사람들 중 몇몇이 말했다. "이 사람은 우리 지도자들이 죽이려고 하는 그 사람이 아니냐?

pt.L: Diziam, pois, alguns dos habitantes de Jerusalém: "Não é este aquele a quem procuram matar?
pt.B: Então alguns dos moradores de Jerusalém diziam: "Não é este o homem que eles estão querendo matar?
pt.R: Algumas pessoas da própria Jerusalém diziam: "Não é este o homem que os nossos líderes querem matar?

am.L: ከኢየሩሳሌም ሰዎችም አንዳንዶቹ እንዲህ ይሉ ነበር፦ «ሊገድሉት የሚፈልጉት ይህ [ሰው] አይደለምን?
am.B: ስለዚህ በኢየሩሳሌም ከሚኖሩት አንዳንዶቹ እንዲህ ይሉ ነበር፦ «ሊገድሉት የሚፈልጉት ሰው ይህ አይደለምን?
am.R: ከኢየሩሳሌም ከተማ የሆኑ አንዳንድ ሰዎች እንዲህ አሉ፦ «መሪዎቻችን ሊገድሉት የሚፈልጉት ሰው ይህ አይደለም?

hi.L: तब यरूशलेम के कुछ निवासी कहने लगे, "क्या यह वही नहीं जिसे वे मार डालने की खोज में हैं?
hi.B: तब यरूशलेम में रहनेवाले कुछ लोग कहने लगे, "क्या यह वही नहीं जिसे वे मार डालना चाहते हैं?
hi.R: यरूशलेम के ही कुछ लोगों ने कहा, "क्या यह वही आदमी नहीं जिसे हमारे अगुवे मार डालना चाहते हैं?

ru.L: Итак, говорили некоторые из иерусалимлян: «Не этого ли они стремятся убить?
ru.B: Тогда некоторые жители Иерусалима говорили: «Разве это не тот, кого они хотят убить?
ru.R: Некоторые люди из самого Иерусалима говорили: «Разве это не тот человек, которого наши вожди хотят убить?

uk.L: Тож деякі з єрусалимців казали: «Хіба це не [той], кого шукають убити?
uk.B: Тож деякі мешканці Єрусалима казали: «Хіба це не той, кого хочуть убити?
uk.R: Деякі люди з самого Єрусалима казали: «Хіба це не той чоловік, якого наші провідники хочуть убити?

ja.L: そこで、エルサレムの人々のうちのある者たちが言っていた。「この人は、彼らが殺そうと求めている者ではないか？
ja.B: そこで、エルサレムに住む人々の中には、こう言う者たちがいた。「これは、あの人たちが殺そうとねらっている人ではないか？
ja.R: エルサレムに住んでいる人たちの中には、こう言う人もいました。「この人は、指導者たちが殺そうとしている人ではないか？

id.L: Lalu beberapa orang Yerusalem berkata, "Bukankah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} ini yang mereka cari untuk dibunuh?
id.B: Beberapa penduduk Yerusalem berkata, "Bukankah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} ini orang yang hendak mereka bunuh?
id.R: Beberapa orang dari Yerusalem sendiri berkata, "Bukankah ini orang yang mau dibunuh oleh para pemimpin kita?

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem: those who live in the city, not the festival crowd
decisions.reason: John uses a word for the city's own residents, not the crowd of pilgrims at the festival. In 7:20 the crowd denied that anyone wanted to kill Jesus; these local people know better. What the authorities intend (5:18; 7:1, 19) is known in Jerusalem itself.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question begins with the negative that looks for agreement: "This is the man, is it not?" The speakers are sure of who he is; what puzzles them is what follows in 7:26.

decisions.choice: they: the authorities who have been trying to kill him
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The people speak of the leaders as a group apart from themselves, the same people whose plan John has reported at 5:18 and 7:1.

decisions.choice: the one (B); the man, our leaders (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the word English needs after "this". Readable names who "they" are, as meaning decision m3 explains; the speakers themselves know who wants Jesus dead. Balanced says "out to kill" for a plan already under way.

decisions.choice: nuestros dirigentes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who "they" are (meaning decision m3). Spanish needs no bracket for "al que".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense where he uses it; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (7:25-36), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("s’écria", "envoyèrent") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("ont dit", "a dit"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je suis venu", "il a fait"). The imperfect ("disaient", "cherchaient") gives the Greek imperfects of what was going on.

decisions.choice: People of Jerusalem speak of Jesus without honorifics ("이 사람", "그")
decisions.reason: The narrator honours Jesus with "께서" and "그분", but characters who do not believe in him speak of him as they would: "이 사람", "그". The difference is the narrator's voice, not a change of meaning. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: ከኢየሩሳሌም ሰዎች (people of Jerusalem, L); በኢየሩሳሌም ከሚኖሩት (those who live in Jerusalem, B); ከኢየሩሳሌም ከተማ የሆኑ (people from the city of Jerusalem, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the city's own residents, as against the festival crowd; Amharic says it with a phrase, since the gentilic form is rare.

decisions.choice: plain "यह", "इसे", "वह" from the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Crowds and opponents speak of Jesus plainly (style guide 7b); the narrator keeps the honorific forms. This holds through the passage.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans for every pronoun for Jesus or God in this passage, and for the expected Christ (7:27, 7:31); "этот" and "тот" plain
decisions.reason: As in English, every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting; the demonstratives the speakers use of Jesus are not pronouns of address and stay plain.

decisions.choice: "エルサレムの人々" (L); "エルサレムに住む人々" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means the city's own residents, not the festival pilgrims (m1). Balanced and Readable say so plainly; "エルサレム人" is not a natural Japanese word. The residents speak plainly among themselves.

source.text: καὶ ἴδε παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγουσιν· μήποτε ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄρχοντες ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;

records.literal_gloss: And look, openly he speaks, and nothing to him they say. Perhaps truly have known the rulers that this is the Christ?

en.L: And look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is speaking openly, and they say nothing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.B: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is speaking in the open, and they say nothing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Can it be that our leaders really know that this man is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.R: But look! He is speaking out where everyone can hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and nobody says anything to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Is it possible that the leaders really have found out that this man is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

es.L: Y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, habla abiertamente, y no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen nada. ¿Será que los gobernantes han reconocido de verdad que este es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, está hablando en público y no {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen nada! ¿Será que nuestros dirigentes de verdad saben que este hombre es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.R: ¡Pero {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}! Está hablando donde todos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pueden oír, y nadie {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice nada. ¿Será posible que los dirigentes de verdad se hayan dado cuenta de que este hombre es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?

fr.L: Et voyez, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parle ouvertement, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent rien. Les chefs auraient-ils vraiment reconnu que celui-ci est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ?
fr.B: Voyez : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parle en public, et on ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit rien ! Nos dirigeants auraient-ils vraiment reconnu que cet homme est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ?
fr.R: Mais regardez ! Il parle devant tout le monde, et personne ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit rien. Est-ce que les chefs auraient vraiment compris que cet homme est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ?

sw.L: Na tazama, anazungumza waziwazi, wala hawamwambii neno. Je, yawezekana kwamba wakuu wamejua kweli kwamba huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.B: Tazama, anazungumza hadharani, wala hawamwambii chochote! Je, yawezekana viongozi wetu wanajua kweli kwamba mtu huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.R: Lakini tazama! Anazungumza mahali ambapo kila mtu anaweza kumsikia, wala hakuna anayemwambia chochote. Je, inawezekana viongozi wamegundua kweli kwamba mtu huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?

vi.L: Kìa, ông ấy đang nói công khai, mà họ chẳng nói gì với ông ấy cả. Có lẽ nào các nhà cầm quyền đã thật biết rằng người này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}?
vi.B: Kìa, ông ấy nói công khai mà họ chẳng nói gì với ông ấy! Hay là các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng ta thật sự biết người này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} rồi sao?
vi.R: Nhưng xem kìa! Ông ấy nói ở nơi mọi người đều nghe được, mà chẳng ai nói gì với ông ấy cả. Có thể nào các nhà lãnh đạo đã thật sự nhận ra người này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} không?

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 그가 드러내 놓고 말하는데, 그들은 그에게 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 혹시 관리들이 이 사람이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}라는 것을 참으로 알게 된 것은 아니겠지?
ko.B: 보아라, 그가 저렇게 드러내 놓고 말하는데도 아무도 그에게 뭐라고 하지 않는다! 혹시 우리 지도자들이 이 사람이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}라는 것을 정말로 알게 된 것인가?
ko.R: 그런데 보아라! 그가 모든 사람이 다 듣는 데서 말하고 있는데, 아무도 그에게 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 혹시 지도자들이 이 사람이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}라는 것을 정말로 알아낸 것일까?

pt.L: E vejam, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fala abertamente, e não {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizem nada. Será que os chefes de fato reconheceram que este é o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}?
pt.B: Vejam, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} está falando em público, e não {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizem nada! Será que os nossos líderes sabem mesmo que este homem é o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}?
pt.R: Mas vejam! Ele está falando onde todo mundo pode ouvi-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, e ninguém diz nada a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Será que os líderes descobriram mesmo que este homem é o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}?

am.L: እነሆም፣ በግልጽ ይናገራል፤ እነርሱም ምንም አይሉትም። አለቆቹ ይህ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} እንደ ሆነ በእውነት አውቀው ይሆንን?
am.B: እነሆ፣ በግልጽ እየተናገረ ነው፤ ምንም አይሉትም! መሪዎቻችን ይህ ሰው {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} መሆኑን በእርግጥ አውቀው ይሆን?
am.R: ነገር ግን ተመልከቱ! ሁሉም በሚሰማበት ቦታ ይናገራል፤ ማንም ግን ምንም አይለውም። መሪዎቹ ይህ ሰው {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} መሆኑን በእርግጥ ተረድተው ይሆን?

hi.L: और देखो, वह खुलेआम बोल रहा है, और वे उससे कुछ नहीं कहते। कहीं ऐसा तो नहीं कि सरदारों ने सचमुच जान लिया है कि यही मसीह है?
hi.B: देखो, वह खुलेआम बोल रहा है, और वे उससे कुछ नहीं कहते! कहीं हमारे अगुवे सचमुच तो नहीं जान गए कि यह आदमी मसीह है?
hi.R: पर देखो! वह ऐसी जगह बोल रहा है जहाँ सब उसे सुन सकते हैं, और कोई उससे कुछ नहीं कहता। क्या ऐसा हो सकता है कि अगुवों को सच में पता चल गया है कि यह आदमी मसीह है?

ru.L: И вот, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} говорит открыто, и ничего {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} не говорят. Неужели начальники и вправду узнали, что это {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}?
ru.B: Смотрите, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} говорит открыто, и {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} ничего не говорят! Неужели наши правители действительно узнали, что этот человек — {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}?
ru.R: Но посмотрите! Он говорит там, где все могут {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} слышать, и никто ничего {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} не говорит. Может быть, наши вожди и правда узнали, что этот человек — {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}?

uk.L: І ось {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} говорить відкрито, і нічого {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} не кажуть. Невже начальники справді пізнали, що це {{christos:Христос|Месія}}?
uk.B: Дивіться, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} говорить відкрито, і ніхто {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} нічого не каже! Невже наші провідники справді знають, що цей чоловік — {{christos:Христос|Месія}}?
uk.R: Але ж подивіться! Він говорить так, що всі чують {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, і ніхто {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} нічого не каже. Невже провідники справді дізналися, що цей чоловік — {{christos:Христос|Месія}}?

ja.L: そして見ろ、彼は公然と語っているのに、彼らは彼に何も言わない。まさか議員たちは、この人が{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}であることを、本当に知ったのだろうか？
ja.B: ほら、あの人は公然と語っているのに、彼らは何も言わない。まさか議員たちは、この人が{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}だと本当に認めたのだろうか？
ja.R: 見てごらん。あの人はみんなの前で話しているのに、だれも何も言わない。もしかして指導者たちは、この人が{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}だと本当に分かったのだろうか？

id.L: Dan lihatlah, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berbicara terang-terangan, dan mereka tidak mengatakan apa pun kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Mungkinkah para pemimpin sungguh-sungguh telah mengetahui bahwa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} inilah {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}}?
id.B: Lihat, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berbicara di depan umum, dan mereka tidak berkata apa-apa kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}! Mungkinkah para pemimpin kita benar-benar tahu bahwa orang ini adalah {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}}?
id.R: Tetapi lihat! Dia berbicara di tempat yang bisa didengar semua orang, dan tidak ada yang berkata apa-apa kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Mungkinkah para pemimpin sungguh-sungguh sudah tahu bahwa orang ini {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}}?

decisions.choice: openly: in public, plainly, without fear
decisions.reason: The word means speaking freely and in the open. It picks up a thread in this chapter: his brothers urged him to show himself openly (7:4), and no one spoke openly about him for fear of the authorities (7:13). Now Jesus himself does what others fear to do.

decisions.choice: a doubtful question: surely the rulers have not come to know this?
decisions.reason: The word that opens the question puts forward something the speakers hardly believe: "Can it be that...?" They are not saying the rulers accept Jesus. They are puzzled that men who want him dead let him speak, and wonder aloud if the rulers have changed their minds. 7:27 shows that they themselves reject the idea.

decisions.choice: the rulers: the leading members of the Jerusalem council
decisions.reason: The same word is used for Nicodemus, "a ruler of the Jews" (3:1), and in 7:48 the Pharisees ask whether any of the rulers has believed in him. They are the men with authority over the temple and the city.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God had promised
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title, not a name: the one God would anoint to rule, whom the people expected (1:20, 41; 4:25). The question is whether Jesus is that person.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself, and pronouns for the expected Christ, since John means Jesus (4:25). At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has "the Christ" as a title, every level writes "the" before the setting, so that the alternative reads "the Messiah" (see the book's terms). This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: our leaders (B); the leaders (R)
decisions.reason: "Rulers" can suggest kings. Balanced and Readable say plainly that these are the people in charge in Jerusalem (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: los gobernantes (L); nuestros dirigentes, los dirigentes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "gobernantes" can suggest kings; these are the leading men of the council (meaning decision m3). "Miren" is spoken to one another, so it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}; deity_pronoun on every pronoun for Jesus or God
decisions.reason: As in 1:20: "the Christ" is a title here (meaning decision m4), so French writes the article outside the span at every level; "est Christ" would read as a name. Every pronoun for Jesus or for God takes the deity_pronoun setting, including "il" and "lui" in the mouths of the crowd, as in English; a pronoun at the start of a sentence ("Il parle", R) is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: auraient-ils vraiment reconnu
decisions.reason: The Greek question doubts what it asks (meaning decision m2). The French conditional of hearsay ("auraient-ils") carries that doubt without extra words.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}
decisions.reason: Korean has no article, so the title stands alone and the predicate ("...라는 것") shows it is a title, not a name. Both forms end in a vowel, so the particles that follow fit either alternative.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the subject honorific ("-시-", "께서") and "그분" in the narrative at every level. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "ông ấy" with no deity_pronoun span when people in the story speak of Jesus
alternatives: "Ngài" under the setting, as the English "he"
decisions.reason: The setting decides how the narrator and the believer write of Jesus; a speaker in the story uses the word a person of the time would use. The people of Jerusalem say "ông ấy" and "người này", nouns of address that take no span. When they speak of the coming Christ (verse 27) they say "Ngài", under the setting.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}
decisions.reason: As the guide sets: "Đấng" marks the title, as "the" does in English ("the Christ"), and the setting gives "Đấng Mê-si-a".

decisions.choice: os chefes
decisions.reason: "Governantes" would suggest a civil government and "príncipes" royalty; "chefes" names the men in charge in Jerusalem (meaning decision m3) while staying close to the Greek word. Balanced and Readable say "líderes", as the English says "leaders".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns (እርሱ, እኔ, the verb endings) are written once, with no span.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span as in the English
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the narrator's honorific forms and by "आप" at every level. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "मसीह", no christos span
decisions.reason: "मसीह" is both the familiar name and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made; Hindi has no article to supply. This applies to 7:27 and 7:31 as well.

decisions.choice: "सरदारों" (L); "हमारे अगुवे", "अगुवों" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The leading members of the Jerusalem council (meaning decision m3), not kings; Balanced and Readable say plainly that they are the leaders.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}, also in verses 27 and 31
decisions.reason: The title takes the christos setting, as in English; Russian has no article, so "это Христос" / "это Мессия" already reads as the title, and both options take the same agreement.

decisions.choice: "начальники" (L); "наши правители" (B); "наши вожди" (R)
decisions.reason: The leading members of the Jerusalem council (meaning decision m3); "князья" would suggest princes.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:Христос|Месія}}" for "the Christ", through John 7
decisions.reason: Ukrainian has no article, so the title is shown by the context ("що цей чоловік — Христос"); both options are masculine nouns, so the words that agree with them read the same under either setting.

decisions.choice: "начальники" (L); "(наші) провідники" (B, R) for the rulers
decisions.reason: The rulers are the leading members of the Jerusalem council (meaning decision m3), not a king or governor, so "правителі" would mislead; "начальники" is the plain literal word.

decisions.choice: "議員たち" (L, B); "指導者たち" (R)
decisions.reason: The rulers are the leading members of the Jerusalem council (m3), the word used of Nicodemus (3:1), so Literal and Balanced say "議員たち". Readable says "指導者たち", the word it uses for the authorities through the chapter. The same choice holds in 7:48.

decisions.choice: "まさか……のだろうか" (L, B); "もしかして……のだろうか" (R)
decisions.reason: The question puts forward something the speakers hardly believe (m2). "まさか" with a question keeps both the doubt and the wondering.

decisions.choice: the belief that the Christ would appear without anyone knowing his origin
alternatives: no one will know his family or birthplace
decisions.reason: The speakers hold a view that the Messiah's origin would be hidden until he appeared. It was not the only view: in 7:42 others say he must come from Bethlehem, David's town. Jewish expectation about the Messiah took several forms, and John reports this one as something some in Jerusalem said.

decisions.choice: irony: they know his earthly home, but not where he truly comes from
decisions.reason: They know he is from Nazareth in Galilee (1:45-46; 7:41, 52). John's readers know that he comes from the Father (1:14; 3:13; 6:38), and Jesus says so in 7:28-29. By their own test, the fact that they do not know his true origin fits his being the Christ.

decisions.choice: no one knows: present tense for what will be true when he comes
decisions.reason: The verb is present, "no one knows", stating a rule about the Christ's coming. The sense is that at his appearing no one will know where he is from.

decisions.choice: will know (B, R); origin (B)
decisions.reason: English uses the future after "when he comes"; Literal keeps the present of the Greek (meaning decision m3). Balanced says "origin" to avoid repeating "where ... from".

decisions.choice: sabrá (B, R); sabe (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the Greek present (meaning decision m3). Spanish needs no pronoun for the coming one ("cuando venga").

decisions.choice: The expected Christ takes the honorific ("께서 오실 때") in the people's speech, while Jesus does not ("이 사람")
decisions.reason: Korean has to choose. The speakers honour the Messiah they expect but not the man in front of them; the contrast keeps the irony of the verse, that the man they speak of plainly is the Christ.

records.literal_gloss: Cried out therefore in the temple teaching the Jesus and saying, "Both me you know, and you know from where I am; and from myself not I have come, but is true the [one] having sent me, whom you not know;

en.L: So Jesus cried out as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the temple, saying, "You know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I am from. And I have not come of {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, but the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true, whom you do not know.
en.B: So Jesus, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the temple courts, cried out, "You know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I come from! Yet I have not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. The one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true, and you do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called out in a loud voice, "So you know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I come from! But I did not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. The one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is real and true. And you do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Clamó, pues, Jesús, enseñando en el templo, y dijo: «Me {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde soy; y no he venido por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, pero el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió es veraz, a quien {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}.
es.B: Entonces Jesús, mientras enseñaba en los atrios del templo, exclamó: «¡Así que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde vengo! Sin embargo, no he venido por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuenta. El que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió es veraz, y {{plural_you:ustedes no|vosotros no}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}}.
es.R: Mientras Jesús enseñaba en el patio del templo, dijo en voz alta: «¡Así que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde vengo! fr.L: Jésus s’écria donc, enseignant dans le temple et disant : « Vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissez, et vous savez d’où je suis ; et je ne suis pas venu de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, mais celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé est vrai, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que vous ne connaissez pas.

fr.R: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait dans la cour du temple, Jésus a dit d’une voix forte : « Ainsi, vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaissez, et vous savez d’où je viens ! decisions.choice: cried out: spoke aloud with solemn force
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for a public proclamation, not a shout of anger: John the Baptist cries out his witness (1:15), and Jesus cries out in 7:37 and 12:44. What follows is said for all to hear.

decisions.choice: a statement with irony: you know me and where I am from, so you think
alternatives: a question: do you know me, and do you know where I am from?
a plain statement that they do know his origin
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a plain statement, as a question ("Do you know me, and do you know where I am from?"), or as an ironic statement. Jesus grants what they said in 7:27, that they know where he is from, and then shows how little they know: he did not come on his own, and they do not know the one who sent him. The irony reading fits the turn that follows with "and yet". A question would make the same point less directly.

decisions.choice: true: real and reliable
decisions.reason: The adjective means genuine, the real thing, and also faithful to his word. It is used of God in 17:3, "the only true God". The one who sent Jesus is real and can be trusted, so Jesus is not a self-appointed messenger.

decisions.choice: you do not know him: they do not know God, who sent Jesus
decisions.reason: The speakers worship God in the temple, yet Jesus says they do not know him. John repeats the charge in 8:19 and 8:55; knowing the Father and knowing the one he sent go together (17:3).

decisions.choice: temple courts (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area, where people gathered and teachers taught, not the sanctuary itself (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own; an exclamation for the irony (B, R); real and true (R)
decisions.reason: "Of myself" is stiff; "on my own" says the same. Balanced and Readable mark the first words as an exclamation to carry the irony (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "real" to show the sense of "true" here.

decisions.choice: ¡Así que ...! (B, R); por mi cuenta
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable mark the first words as an exclamation to carry the irony (meaning decision m2), whose footnote gives the other readings.

decisions.choice: they tried: an attempt that did not succeed; the subject is not named
decisions.reason: The tense describes an effort under way. John does not say who "they" were: hostile people in the crowd, or those who spoke for the authorities. In 7:32 the authorities act formally by sending officers.

decisions.choice: laid a hand on him: arrested him
decisions.reason: To lay a hand on someone means to take hold of him by force. The same phrase comes again in 7:44, and 8:20 says the same thing in other words.

decisions.choice: his hour: the appointed time of his death and glorification
decisions.reason: Jesus has said that his hour has not yet come (2:4) and that his time is not yet here (7:6, 8). The hour is the time the Father has set for his death and return to glory (12:23; 13:1; 17:1). Until then no one can seize him; 8:20 says this again.

decisions.choice: took hold of (B); touched, time, some people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what laying a hand on someone means (meaning decision m2). Readable says "time" for the appointed hour, as the book's terms allow, and "some people" for the unnamed subject (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: hora at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Spanish "su hora" is everyday language for an appointed time, so Readable keeps it; the different word of 7:6-8 is "tiempo".

decisions.choice: mettre la main sur lui (L, B)
decisions.reason: French "mettre la main sur quelqu’un" is the same idiom as the Greek and means to seize or arrest (meaning decision m2), so Balanced can keep it where the English Balanced must explain it. Readable says "touché", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: son heure at every level (Readable too)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: English Readable says "time" because "hour" sounds like sixty minutes, but French "son heure n’était pas encore venue" is everyday language for an appointed moment, so Readable keeps the word and the thread through the Gospel (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "때" for hour (hora) at every level
decisions.reason: "그분의 때" is the natural Korean for an appointed time and keeps the thread of Jesus's "hour" through the book. Korean uses the same word for "my time" (kairos) in 7:6 and 7:8, so the two Greek words are not told apart.

decisions.choice: giờ (hour), at every level
decisions.reason: "giờ" keeps the thread of Jesus's hour (2:4; 12:23; 13:1; 17:1) and stays distinct from "thời điểm", used for the brothers' "time" in 7:6-8. It is plain enough for Readable, so Vietnamese does not need the English Readable's "time".

decisions.choice: a hora dele (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "time" because "his hour" is unclear in English. In Portuguese "chegou a hora dele" is everyday speech for the appointed moment, including the moment of death, so Readable keeps "hora" with the other levels and the thread of the book's "hour" stays visible.

decisions.choice: ሰዓቱ (his hour, L, B); ጊዜው (his time, R)
decisions.reason: Hour is the thread of Jesus's appointed time through John; Literal and Balanced keep ሰዓት so the thread stays visible, Readable says ጊዜ, as the book's terms note sets for English.

decisions.choice: "घड़ी" (L, B); "समय" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's appointed hour (meaning decision m3): "घड़ी" keeps John's thread of the hour at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "his time", as the book's terms allow.

decisions.choice: passive "कोशिश की गई" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek does not name who tried (meaning decision m1); with the honorific plural for Jesus, "उन्होंने उन्हें" would be unclear, so Balanced uses the passive.

decisions.choice: "час" (L, B); "время" (R)
decisions.reason: The appointed time of his death and glorification (meaning decision m3). The book's terms keep "hour" at Literal and Balanced so the thread stays visible; Readable may say "время".

decisions.choice: "時" (every level)
alternatives: "時機", the word used for 7:6 and 7:8
decisions.reason: The book's terms keep "時" for Jesus's appointed hour (m3), so the thread from 2:4 to 12:23 and 17:1 stays visible; the different word of 7:6 and 7:8 is "時機". The same holds in 8:20.

sw.R: Lakini watu wengi katika umati walimwamini. Wakasema, "{{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakapokuja, je, atafanya ishara nyingi kuliko alizofanya mtu huyu? Hapana!"

vi.L: Nhưng trong đám đông có nhiều người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ nói: "Khi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đến, chẳng lẽ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm nhiều dấu lạ hơn những [dấu lạ] người này đã làm sao?"
vi.B: Thế nhưng trong đám đông có nhiều người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ cứ nói: "Khi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đâu có làm nhiều dấu lạ hơn người này đã làm, phải không?"
vi.R: Nhưng nhiều người trong đám đông tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Khi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có làm nhiều dấu lạ hơn người này không? Chắc chắn là không!"

ko.L: 그러나 무리 가운데 많은 이가 그분을 믿었고, 말하고 있었다. "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 오실 때에, 이 [사람이] 행한 것보다 더 많은 표적을 행하시겠느냐?"
ko.B: 그러나 무리 가운데 많은 사람이 그분을 믿었다. 그들은 "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 오신다 해도, 이 사람이 행한 것보다 더 많은 표적을 행하시지는 않을 것이다. 그렇지 않으냐?" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 그러나 무리 가운데 많은 사람이 예수님을 믿었다. 그들이 말했다. "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 오신다고 해도, 이 사람이 한 것보다 더 많은 표적을 행하시겠느냐? 그렇지 않을 것이다!"

pt.L: Mas muitos da multidão creram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} e diziam: "Quando o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} vier, fará {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mais sinais do que os que este [homem] fez?"
pt.B: Muitos da multidão, porém, creram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} e diziam: "Quando o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} vier, por acaso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fará mais sinais do que este homem fez?"
pt.R: Mas muitas pessoas da multidão acreditaram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Elas diziam: "Quando o {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} vier, será que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} vai fazer mais sinais do que este homem fez? Claro que não!"

am.L: ከሕዝቡም ብዙዎች በእርሱ አመኑ፤ እንዲህም ይሉ ነበር፦ «{{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በሚመጣበት ጊዜ ይህ [ሰው] ካደረጋቸው የሚበልጡ ምልክቶችን ያደርጋልን?»
am.B: ሆኖም ከሕዝቡ መካከል ብዙዎች በእርሱ አመኑ፤ እንዲህም ይሉ ነበር፦ «{{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ሲመጣ ይህ ሰው ካደረጋቸው የሚበልጡ ምልክቶችን ያደርጋል ብለን እንጠብቃለን?»
am.R: ነገር ግን በሕዝቡ መካከል የነበሩ ብዙ ሰዎች በእርሱ አመኑ። እንዲህም አሉ፦ «{{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ሲመጣ ይህ ሰው ካደረጋቸው የሚበልጡ ምልክቶችን ያደርጋል? በፍጹም!»

hi.L: पर भीड़ में से बहुतों ने उन पर विश्वास किया, और कहने लगे, "मसीह जब आएगा, तो क्या वह इससे अधिक चिह्न करेगा जितने इसने किए हैं?"
hi.B: फिर भी भीड़ में से बहुत लोगों ने उन पर विश्वास किया, और वे कहते रहे, "जब मसीह आएगा, तो वह इस आदमी से अधिक चिह्न तो नहीं दिखाएगा, है न?"
hi.R: पर भीड़ में से बहुत लोगों ने उन पर विश्वास किया। उन्होंने कहा, "जब मसीह आएगा, तो क्या वह इस आदमी से ज़्यादा चिह्न दिखाएगा? बिलकुल नहीं!"

ru.L: Из толпы же многие поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} и говорили: «Когда придёт {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}, разве {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} совершит больше знамений, чем совершил этот?»
ru.B: Однако многие в толпе поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} и говорили: «Когда придёт {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} ведь не совершит больше знамений, чем этот человек, правда?»
ru.R: Но многие люди в толпе поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}. Они говорили: «Когда придёт {{christos:Христос|Мессия}}, разве {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} совершит больше знаков, чем этот человек? Конечно, нет!»

uk.L: А багато з натовпу повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і казали: «Коли прийде {{christos:Христос|Месія}}, чи зробить {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} більше знаків, ніж цей зробив?»
uk.B: Проте багато людей з натовпу повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і казали: «Коли прийде {{christos:Христос|Месія}}, хіба {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробить більше знаків, ніж зробив цей чоловік?»
uk.R: Але багато людей у натовпі повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}. Вони казали: «Коли прийде {{christos:Христос|Месія}}, хіба {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробить більше знаків, ніж цей чоловік? Звісно, ні!»

ja.L: しかし、群衆の中から多くの者がイエスを信じた。そして言っていた。「{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}が来るとき、この人が行ったよりも多くのしるしを行うだろうか？」
ja.B: しかし、群衆の中の多くの人々がイエスを信じて、「{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}が来ても、この人が行ったより多くのしるしを行うことはないだろう？」と言い続けた。
ja.R: でも、群衆の中の多くの人がイエスを信じました。そして「{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}が来ても、この人よりもたくさんのしるしを行うだろうか？そんなことはないだろう」と言いました。

id.L: Tetapi banyak dari orang banyak itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, dan mereka berkata, "Apabila {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}} datang, apakah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} akan melakukan lebih banyak tanda daripada yang telah dilakukan orang ini?"
id.B: Namun banyak orang di antara orang banyak itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, dan mereka terus berkata, "Kalau {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}} datang, tentu {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tidak akan melakukan lebih banyak tanda daripada yang telah dilakukan orang ini, bukan?"
id.R: Tetapi banyak orang di antara orang banyak itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Mereka berkata, "Kalau {{christos:Kristus|Mesias}} datang, apakah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} akan melakukan lebih banyak tanda daripada orang ini? Tidak mungkin!"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question opens with the negative that looks for "no": the Christ could hardly do more signs than this man has. The speakers are close to saying that Jesus is the Christ.

decisions.choice: believed in him: a real but early belief
decisions.reason: John uses the same words for true faith (3:16) and for belief that does not yet go deep (2:23-25; 8:30-31). Here belief rests on his signs; it stands against the hostility of 7:30.

decisions.choice: signs: deeds that point to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: John calls Jesus's works signs because they show his glory and lead people to believe (2:11; 20:30-31). In Jerusalem he had healed the man at the pool (5:1-9), and others had seen his signs at the Passover (2:23).

decisions.choice: a tag question (B); an added "Surely not!" (R)
decisions.reason: English shows that a "no" is expected (meaning decision m1) with "will he?" at the end, or with a short reply. Literal keeps a plain question.

decisions.choice: ¿acaso ...? (B); ¡Seguro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that the question expects "no" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: ne fera tout de même pas ... ?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no (meaning decision m1). French shows this with a negative statement turned into a question by "tout de même", where English uses a tag question; Readable adds a short answer, as in English.

decisions.choice: por acaso ... ?
decisions.reason: Portuguese marks a question that expects "no" (meaning decision m1) with "por acaso" more naturally than with a tag question, which the English uses.

decisions.choice: ምልክቶች (signs) at every level
decisions.reason: John's word points beyond the deed to who Jesus is; ምልክት keeps that, while ተአምር would name only the wonder. The same word through the book.

decisions.choice: "चिह्न"
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for John's "sign", deeds that point to who Jesus is (meaning decision m3), never "चमत्कार".

decisions.choice: "знамений" (L, B); "знаков" (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide key term for John, never "чудо": deeds that point to who Jesus is (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τοῦ ὄχλου γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὑπηρέτας ἵνα πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Heard the Pharisees the crowd muttering about him these things, and sent the chief priests and the Pharisees officers that they might seize him.

en.L: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees heard the crowd talking quietly about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in this way, so the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple police to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The Pharisees heard what the people in the crowd were saying quietly about Jesus. So the leading priests and the Pharisees sent some temple guards to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away.

es.L: Oyeron los fariseos a la multitud que murmuraba estas cosas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y los principales sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron alguaciles para prenderlo.
es.B: Los fariseos oyeron que la multitud murmuraba esto acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, así que los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron a los guardias del templo para arrestarlo.
es.R: Los fariseos oyeron lo que la gente decía en voz baja acerca de Jesús. Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron a unos guardias del templo para que se {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaran.

fr.L: Les Pharisiens entendirent la foule murmurer ces choses à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet, et les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens envoyèrent des gardes pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} saisir.
fr.B: Les Pharisiens entendirent la foule chuchoter ainsi à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet ; alors les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens envoyèrent des gardes du temple pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}arrêter.
fr.R: Les Pharisiens ont entendu ce que les gens de la foule disaient tout bas sur Jésus. Alors les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens ont envoyé des gardes du temple pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmener.

sw.L: Mafarisayo waliusikia umati ukinung'unika mambo haya juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma watumishi wamkamate.
sw.B: Mafarisayo waliusikia umati ukinong'ona hivyo juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, basi wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma walinzi wa hekalu wamkamate.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walisikia yale watu katika umati waliyokuwa wakinong'ona juu ya Yesu. Basi viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma baadhi ya walinzi wa hekalu wamchukue.

vi.L: Người Pha-ri-si nghe đám đông xì xào những điều ấy về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các thầy tế lễ cả cùng người Pha-ri-si sai các cảnh vệ đi bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Người Pha-ri-si nghe đám đông thì thầm bàn tán như vậy về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nên các thầy tế lễ cả và người Pha-ri-si sai lính canh đền thờ đi bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người Pha-ri-si nghe dân chúng thì thầm với nhau về Đức Giê-xu. Vì vậy các thầy tế lễ cả và những người Pha-ri-si sai mấy người lính canh đền thờ đi bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 바리새파 사람들이 무리가 그분에 대하여 이런 것들을 수군거리는 것을 들었다. 그리고 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 그분을 잡으려고 경비병들을 보냈다.
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들은 무리가 그분에 대해 이렇게 수군거리는 것을 들었다. 그래서 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들이 그분을 체포하려고 성전 경비병들을 보냈다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들은 무리 가운데 사람들이 예수님에 대해 몰래 하는 말을 들었다. 그래서 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들은 예수님을 잡아 오라고 성전 경비병들을 보냈다.

pt.L: Os fariseus ouviram a multidão murmurando essas coisas a respeito {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, e os chefes dos sacerdotes e os fariseus enviaram servidores para prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
pt.B: Os fariseus ouviram a multidão comentando essas coisas em voz baixa a respeito {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}; então os chefes dos sacerdotes e os fariseus mandaram guardas do templo para prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
pt.R: Os fariseus ouviram o que o povo na multidão estava dizendo baixinho sobre Jesus. Então os chefes dos sacerdotes e os fariseus mandaram alguns guardas do templo para levá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} preso.

am.L: ፈሪሳውያን ሕዝቡ ስለ እርሱ ይህን ሲያንሾካሹኩ ሰሙ፤ የካህናት አለቆችና ፈሪሳውያንም ሊይዙት አገልጋዮችን ላኩ።
am.B: ፈሪሳውያን ሕዝቡ ስለ እርሱ እንዲህ እያሉ ሲያንሾካሹኩ ሰሙ፤ ስለዚህ የካህናት አለቆችና ፈሪሳውያን እንዲይዙት የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎችን ላኩ።
am.R: ፈሪሳውያን ሕዝቡ ስለ ኢየሱስ በሹክሹክታ የሚሉትን ሰሙ። ስለዚህ የካህናት አለቆችና ፈሪሳውያን ኢየሱስን ይዘው እንዲወስዱት አንዳንድ የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎችን ላኩ።

hi.L: फ़रीसियों ने भीड़ को उनके विषय में ये बातें कानाफूसी करते सुना, और प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों ने उन्हें पकड़ने के लिए सिपाही भेजे।
hi.B: फ़रीसियों ने सुना कि भीड़ उनके बारे में दबी आवाज़ में ऐसी बातें कर रही है, इसलिए प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों ने उन्हें गिरफ़्तार करने के लिए मन्दिर के पहरेदार भेजे।
hi.R: फ़रीसियों ने सुना कि भीड़ के लोग यीशु के बारे में धीरे-धीरे क्या कह रहे हैं। इसलिए प्रधान याजकों और फ़रीसियों ने यीशु को पकड़ ले जाने के लिए मन्दिर के कुछ पहरेदार भेजे।

ru.L: Фарисеи услышали, что толпа шепчет о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} такое, и старшие священники и фарисеи послали служителей схватить {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.B: Фарисеи услышали, как люди в толпе тихо переговариваются о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}}, и старшие священники и фарисеи послали храмовую стражу арестовать {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.
ru.R: Фарисеи услышали, что люди в толпе тихо говорят об Иисусе. Тогда старшие священники и фарисеи послали храмовых стражников схватить {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}.

uk.L: Почули фарисеї, що натовп перешіптується про {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} таке, і старші священники та фарисеї послали прислужників, щоб схопити {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.
uk.B: Фарисеї почули, як натовп стиха перемовляється про {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, тож старші священники й фарисеї послали храмових вартових, щоб заарештувати {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.

id.R: Orang-orang Farisi mendengar apa yang dibisikkan orang banyak tentang Yesus. Jadi imam-imam kepala dan orang-orang Farisi menyuruh beberapa penjaga Bait Allah untuk menangkap {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}.

decisions.choice: muttering: talking in low voices
decisions.reason: The verb means talk under one's breath. It can mean grumbling, as in 6:41, but here, as in 7:12, it is the crowd's quiet talk about whether Jesus is the Christ. The Pharisees hear the favorable talk of 7:31.

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the Pharisees: the council's leading members
decisions.reason: The chief priests were the high priest and the leading men of the priestly families who ran the temple. Together with the Pharisees among them they made up the Jerusalem council; John names the two groups together in 7:45, 11:47, 11:57 and 18:3.

decisions.choice: officers: the temple police serving the council
decisions.reason: The word means attendants or assistants. Here they are the men who kept order in the temple for the chief priests. They come back empty-handed in 7:45-46, and they arrest Jesus in 18:3, 12.

decisions.choice: temple police (B); temple guards, take him away (R); leading priests (R)
decisions.reason: "Officers" alone does not say whose officers these are. Balanced and Readable name their role (meaning decision m3). Readable says "leading priests" so that "chief" is not taken as a single leader.

decisions.choice: alguaciles (L); guardias del templo (B, R); jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: names whose officers these were (meaning decision m3). "Murmurar" covers quiet talk as in 7:12.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); des gardes (L); des gardes du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide French terms for John. "Les chefs des prêtres" says that several leading priests are meant, so Readable does not need the English "leading" to avoid a single chief. French "officier" is a military rank and "huissier" a court usher today, so "gardes" names the council's temple police (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable add "du temple", as English does.

decisions.choice: "경비병들" (L); "성전 경비병들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The men sent are the temple police who served the council; "하인들" (servants) would hide that they came to make an arrest.

decisions.choice: các thầy tế lễ cả; cảnh vệ (L), lính canh đền thờ (B, R)
decisions.reason: "thầy tế lễ cả" is the established Protestant term for the chief priests ("thượng tế" is the Catholic one). The officers were the temple police: Literal says "cảnh vệ" (guards); Balanced and Readable say whose guards they were.

decisions.choice: servidores (L); guardas do templo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "oficiais" suggests military officers. Literal says "servidores", the attendants the Greek word names; Balanced and Readable name their role, "guardas do templo" (meaning decision m3). "Os chefes dos sacerdotes" is the term for the whole New Testament at every level (style section 6).

decisions.choice: ሲያንሾካሹኩ, በሹክሹክታ (whispering, talking low)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as low-voiced talk, not complaint; ማጉረምረም would make the crowd discontented.

decisions.choice: አገልጋዮች (attendants, L); የቤተ መቅደስ ጠባቂዎች (temple guards, B, R)
decisions.reason: They were the council's temple police, not Roman soldiers; Literal keeps the general word for men in service.

decisions.choice: "सिपाही" (L); "मन्दिर के पहरेदार" (B, R)
decisions.reason: These were the temple police serving the council (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable name their role. "कानाफूसी" is the word of 7:12 for the same Greek verb.

decisions.choice: "старшие священники"
decisions.reason: The Synodal plural "первосвященники" blurs the one high priest with the leading priests (style guide, section 6).

decisions.choice: "служителей" (L); "храмовую стражу" (B); "храмовых стражников" (R)
decisions.reason: The temple police serving the council (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable name their role.

decisions.choice: "старші священники" for the chief priests; "прислужники" (L), "храмові вартові" (B, R) for the officers, also in verses 45-46
decisions.reason: As set for the Gospels: "первосвященики" would blur the leading priests with the one high priest. The officers are the temple police serving the council (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "下役たち" (L); "神殿の警備兵たち" (B, R), as in 18:3-22 and 19:6
decisions.reason: The officers are the men who kept order in the temple for the chief priests (m3). "下役" is the word for an attendant who carries out orders; Balanced and Readable say plainly who they were. The same choice holds in 7:45-46 and in the arrest and trial (18:3, 12, 18, 22; 19:6).

decisions.choice: "penjaga-penjaga Bait Allah" (B, R)
decisions.reason: m3: the officers were the temple police serving the council. "penjaga Bait Allah" names what they were in plain Indonesian; "imam-imam kepala" is the glossary term for the chief priests (Terms, section 3).

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus, "Yet time little with you I am, and I go to the [one] having sent me.

en.L: So Jesus said, "Yet a little time I am with you, and [then] I go to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

vi.B: Vậy Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ta còn ở với các người thêm ít lâu nữa, rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi về cùng Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "아직 잠시 동안 내가 너희와 함께 있고, [그 다음에] 나를 보내신 분께로 간다.

pt.L: Disse, então, Jesus: "Ainda um pouco de tempo estou com vocês, e [depois] vou para aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.
pt.B: Então Jesus disse: "Por pouco tempo ainda estou com vocês; depois vou embora para aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.

ru.L: Итак, сказал Иисус: «Ещё недолгое время {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} с вами, и [потом] иду к тому, кто {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} послал.

uk.L: Тож сказав Ісус: «Ще недовгий час {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} з вами, і [тоді] йду до того, хто послав {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}.

decisions.choice: a little while: the short time left before his death
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the time left before he is taken from them. He says the same to the crowd in 12:35 and to his disciples in 13:33 and 16:16-19. The officers have just been sent to arrest him, but the timing is his, not theirs (7:30).

decisions.choice: I go: I go away, return to the Father
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for Jesus's departure to the Father through his death and resurrection (8:14, 21; 13:3, 33; 16:5). He came from the one who sent him (7:29) and goes back to him.

decisions.choice: then (all levels); go away (B); go back (R)
decisions.reason: The "and" joins two stages: first a little time with them, then his going. English shows the order with "then", bracketed in Literal. Balanced says "go away" for John's word of departure (meaning decision m2); Readable says "go back", since he came from the Father (7:29).

decisions.choice: [luego] (L); luego, después (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the two stages (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: where I am: the present tense for where he will be with the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "where I will be" but "where I am". He speaks of the Father's presence as his own place, where he belongs already (1:18; 17:24; also 12:26 and 14:3). The emphatic "I" is set against "you". Some readers also hear in the words his "I am" sayings; here the plain sense of place comes first.

decisions.choice: you will seek me and not find me: when it is too late
decisions.reason: They are seeking him now to kill him (7:1, 25, 30). A time will come when they look for him and he is gone. In 8:21 Jesus adds that they will die in their sin. He says the same words to his disciples in 13:33, but promises to come back for them (14:3).

decisions.choice: a possible echo of Wisdom's warning in Proverbs
decisions.reason: In Proverbs 1:28 Wisdom says that those who rejected her will seek her and not find her. The words are close, and John elsewhere presents Jesus in terms used of God's wisdom, but the passage does not quote Proverbs, and the echo may not be intended.

decisions.choice: search for (B); look for (R)
decisions.reason: "Seek" is less common in speech; Balanced and Readable use everyday words, as at 6:24. They repeat "me", which Literal brackets, and put "where I am" after the verb, the usual English order.

decisions.choice: no me encontrarán, no supplied word
decisions.reason: Spanish needs the object clitic "me" with "encontrar", so Literal needs no bracket.

decisions.choice: chercher at every level
decisions.reason: French "chercher" is both the plain word and the word for "seek", so every level can keep it where the English moves from "seek" to "search for" and "look for"; this keeps the echo of 7:36 and 13:33.

decisions.choice: "わたしがいる所" (present, every level)
decisions.reason: Jesus says "where I am", not "where I will be" (m1). Every level keeps the present, and 7:36 repeats the words exactly.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the authorities and those around them who oppose Jesus
alternatives: the listeners in the temple generally
decisions.reason: Jesus has just spoken to the officers sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees (7:32) and to those who seek him (7:34). Those who reply take his words as being about them, the ones who would be searching for him. In this chapter "the Jews" are the authorities who seek to kill him (7:1, 11, 13). They may include people in the temple who sided with them; it is not the people as a whole, since the crowd, the people of Jerusalem and Jesus himself are all Jews.

decisions.choice: they misunderstand: they think of a journey, he means his return to the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke of going to the one who sent him (7:33). His hearers think only of places on a map, where he might go out of their reach. John often lets hearers take Jesus's words on the wrong level (3:4; 4:11; 6:52); 8:22 repeats the misunderstanding in a darker form.

decisions.choice: a scornful question that expects no
decisions.reason: The question begins with the negative that looks for "no". The speakers mock the idea: a teacher of Israel would hardly leave the land to teach foreigners.

decisions.choice: the Dispersion among the Greeks: Jews living outside the land in the Greek-speaking world
decisions.reason: The word means "scattering" and was used for the Jewish communities living outside the land of Israel. "Of the Greeks" says where they were scattered: among the Greek-speaking peoples around the eastern Mediterranean.

decisions.choice: the Greeks: non-Jews, people of Greek language and culture
decisions.reason: "The Greeks" here stands for Gentiles in general, the peoples among whom the Dispersion lived. Some take it to mean Greek-speaking Jews, but the speakers have just named the Jews of the Dispersion; the further step, teaching the Greeks themselves, is the point of the scorn. In 12:20 the word is used of Greeks who came up to worship at the festival.

decisions.choice: irony: what they mock comes true
decisions.reason: The speakers mean the idea as an absurdity, but John's readers know that it happens: Greeks come seeking Jesus as his hour arrives (12:20-23), and he has other sheep to gather (10:16; 11:52). Through his disciples his teaching reached the Greeks.

decisions.choice: the Jews scattered among the Greeks (B); the Jews who live far away in Greek lands (R)
decisions.reason: "The Dispersion" is a technical term most readers will not know. Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m2). Balanced puts the expected "no" into "surely ... not"; Readable adds a short answer.

decisions.choice: los judíos que viven dispersos entre los griegos (B); los judíos que viven lejos, en tierras griegas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "la Dispersión" is a technical term; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: la Dispersion (L); les Juifs dispersés parmi les Grecs (B); les Juifs qui vivent loin d’ici, dans les pays grecs (R)
decisions.reason: "La diaspora" is a familiar French word, but it now names any community living abroad and would sound modern here. Literal keeps the old technical term "la Dispersion"; Balanced and Readable say who is meant (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Wagiriki
decisions.reason: "Wayunani" is the older Bible word for Greeks; "Wagiriki" is the word readers use today. The meaning note explains that non-Jews of Greek language and culture are meant.

decisions.choice: "그리스 사람들 가운데 흩어져 사는 [이들]" (L); "... 유대인들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "디아스포라" is a loanword many readers will not know, so every level describes the scattered Jews. "그리스 사람" is the guide's word for Hellenes; the older "헬라인" is familiar from earlier Bibles but no longer everyday Korean.

decisions.choice: በግሪኮች መካከል ወደ ተበተኑት [አይሁድ] (to the [Jews] scattered among the Greeks)
alternatives: ወደ ግሪኮች ስደት (to the dispersion of the Greeks)
decisions.reason: Amharic has no current noun for the Dispersion; the participle 'scattered' says it, and the people meant are bracketed.

decisions.choice: "बिखरे हुओं" (L); "बिखरे हुए यहूदियों" (B); "दूर यूनानी देशों में रहनेवाले यहूदियों" (R)
decisions.reason: "The Dispersion" is a technical term (meaning decision m2); every level says what it was, Balanced and Readable naming the Jews meant. "कहीं ... तो नहीं" shows that the question expects "no" (m1).

decisions.choice: "рассеяние" (L); "иудеям, рассеянным среди греков" (B); "иудеям, которые живут далеко, в греческих странах" (R)
decisions.reason: Jews living outside the land in the Greek-speaking world (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say what the term means.

decisions.choice: "розсіяння серед еллінів" (L); "юдеї, розсіяні серед греків" (B); "греки" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greeks here are non-Jews of Greek language and culture (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps "елліни", as the style guide sets, and Balanced and Readable say "греки" and name the Jews living among them (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "離散の民" (L); "散らされている同胞" (B); "遠くのギリシア人の国々に住んでいるユダヤ人" (R)
decisions.reason: The word names the Jewish communities living outside the land (m2). Literal keeps the noun "離散"; Balanced and Readable say who they were. "まさか……あるまい" carries the scorn of a question that expects no (m1).

decisions.choice: word: saying; they ask what it means
decisions.reason: "What is this word" asks about the meaning of what Jesus said. The speakers repeat his words exactly as 7:34 has them, which shows they heard him clearly but cannot make sense of them.

decisions.choice: the repetition stresses their failure to understand
decisions.reason: John repeats the whole saying so the reader sees its weight. The question is left without an answer; the reader knows that he goes to the Father (7:33). Even the disciples later ask a similar question (16:17-18).

decisions.choice: What is this saying of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} (B); What does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mean (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek asks what this word is. Balanced calls it a saying; Readable asks what he means. Both repeat the words exactly as each level gave them in 7:34.

decisions.choice: the saying repeated exactly as in 7:34
decisions.reason: As in English: every level repeats Jesus's words exactly, so the reader sees their weight (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: The quoted saying comes first, then "하고 그가 말한 이 말"
decisions.reason: Korean puts a quotation before the verb of saying, so the saying moves to the front of the question.

decisions.choice: the quoted saying comes first, then 'what is this word'
alternatives: What is this word ... followed by the quotation, as in Greek
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb of saying after its quotation; the question about the saying closes the sentence.

decisions.choice: the repeated saying first, then the question ("……と言ったこの言葉は、何なのか")
alternatives: the question first, then the saying
decisions.reason: Japanese puts a quoted saying before the words that refer to it. The saying is repeated word for word from 7:34 at each level, as the Greek repeats it (m1).
